observed_result.audio_blocks: Each block is 256 samples decoded by the fixed clamp to [-1, 1]; the samples are mono 16-bit PCM at 8,000 Hz with exactly 3 x 256 = 768 frames (checked on samples/high_pulse.wav).
observed_result.held_out: high pulse is judged high steady by both groups in every seed: the pitch carries over, the unseen pattern pairing does not.
observed_result.capacity_split: encoder 96, core 5,280, readout 16,384, decoder 0 parameters; the frozen-core group does not train the core.
observed_result.reading: The core generates restorable audio blocks at the right rate and length and learns six or seven of eight seen conditions; the frozen-core control does as well or slightly better, so the core's learning is not shown to matter here. Repeating the prompt's last word keeps the judged condition over all three blocks for only 2 to 6 of 9 prompts. The held-out condition is not generated correctly.
observed_result.reproducibility: The rerun at the same commit produced byte-identical media.json, summary.txt and WAV samples.

assumption_statement: Pixel or sample MSE says nothing about perceptual quality. This proves generation on a finite fixture of nine conditions, not open-ended image or audio generation. The decoder is a fixed clamp with no parameters; the prompt reaches the output only through the core. The frozen-core control trains only the encoder and readout, showing what the periphery alone can do with the same budget. (The four assumptions RunMedia writes into media.json.)
limitations: Nine synthetic tones of three pitches and three envelopes; no claim about speech, music or perceptual quality.
The held-out condition is generated wrongly in every seed (high steady instead of high pulse).
The frozen-core control matches or beats the trained core; the core's learning is not shown to matter on this fixture.
Temporal consistency over three blocks is partial (2 to 6 of 9 prompts).
Real authorised audio data is TSK-11 and remains blocked_data.
